messages:
mike_support: Customer in finance corp using Private (VPC) deployment reports API failures from their on-prem inference gateway after switching to a company-wide proxy + PAC. They say 'works from home, fails from office'.
elaine_sre: thanks. can you paste the exact error the customer sees from their app or curl? also which endpoints are failing (api.redwood-inference.com or private-hosted?)
mike_support: It's to their Private control plane (customer-managed hostnames) over TLS. App logs show repeated TLS handshake errors and 502/504 when the client talks to the control plane. Curl from a dev machine behind corp proxy returns: `curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` and `curl -v` shows CONNECT to hostname succeeds but TLS handshake fails (alert: unknown certificate). They mentioned the proxy does TLS inspect with company CA.
elaine_sre: two quick suspects: 1) TLS MITM (inspect) breaking client cert validation or OCSP stapling; 2) PAC or proxy rules rewriting CONNECT so SNI is lost. ask them for `openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -servername <host> -showcerts` output from behind proxy (if proxy allows direct TLS). if not possible, `curl --proxy-insecure --proxy <proxy> -v https://<host>/health` might show more.
raj_infra: adding: if the proxy is terminating TLS, it must re-sign certs with a company CA that clients trust. But our Private control plane expects mutual TLS for some endpoints — if the proxy strips or re-signs the client cert, auth will fail. Also SNI must be preserved for routing to the right backend in their VPC.
mike_support: customer ran `openssl s_client` via a jump host (office) and attached snippet:
```
CONNECTED(00000005)
139812345678912:error:1400410B:SSL routines:CONNECT_CR_SRVR_HELLO:wrong version number:s3_clnt.c:???
---
No peer certificate available
---
```
They also ran curl with `--proxy http://proxy.corp:8080` and got `error: SSL certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain`.
elaine_sre: ok that matches TLS inspect re-signing. two viable paths: 1) allow TLS passthrough for the control plane hostnames (proxy should do CONNECT and not inspect) — preserves cert chain & SNI; OR 2) if org policy requires inspection, they must install the inspection CA into their VMs and ensure OCSP/CRL access to validate stapled certs. but the mutual-auth endpoints will still fail if the proxy strips client certs.
mike_support: customer says corporate security won't disable inspection globally. they asked if we can add our control-plane hostnames to an allowlist so the proxy can bypass MITM for just these domains.
raj_infra: that's the recommended approach. provide the following to the customer firewall/proxy team:
- hostnames to allow CONNECT passthrough (no TLS inspect):
  - controlplane.customer-redwood.example.com
  - api.customer-redwood.example.com
- ports: 443 (egress)
- ensure proxy allows SNI passthrough and does not rewrite/strip `CONNECT` or client certificate bytes
- if they use a PAC file, confirm the PAC returns `DIRECT` for these hostnames (example rule):
```
function FindProxyForURL(url, host) {
  if (shExpMatch(host, "*.customer-redwood.example.com")) return "DIRECT";
  return "PROXY proxy.corp:8080";
}
```
mike_support: customer tried to set PAC but reported their browser works after PAC change, but their on-prem inference gateway (java service) still fails. they said the gateway uses a JVM-level proxy config and didn't pick up the PAC.
elaine_sre: JVM PAC support is limited. For services, best is to configure the process to either use a direct outbound route to the egress gateway or configure `-Dhttps.proxyHost` and `-Dhttps.proxyPort` and import the company CA into the JVM truststore. but again, for passthrough you want the proxy to allow CONNECT and not MITM.
raj_infra: also verify DNS resolution: some proxies intercept DNS and respond with internal IPs. ask for `nslookup controlplane.customer-redwood.example.com` from the gateway and from a working host, compare results. if DNS split-horizon resolves to internal IPs that the gateway cannot route to, that'll break.
mike_support: customer ran `nslookup` and got same external IP from both hosts. traceroute from gateway shows `10.10.1.1` (proxy) as next hop then `* * *` after — they said proxy returns reset for large TLS handshakes (we suspect the proxy inspects and chokes on client cert size).
elaine_sre: possible. ask for `curl --trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 https://controlplane.customer-redwood.example.com/health` and the trace file. also ask for `strace` of the gateway process when it fails (if they can) to capture socket errors.
mike_support: customer attached `curl --trace` showing `* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):` then `* SSL certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain` — again points to MITM.
egress-proxy-bot: healthcheck alert: egress-check for customer-vpc failed 3/3 — code 495 (tls_inspect_block) at 2024-11-17T09:12:03Z :warning:
elaine_sre: filing infra ticket to request we add guidance + sample PAC and allowlist for customers with on-prem gateways. ticket INFRA-5408. mike, assign to raj for any follow ups with IP ranges.
raj_infra: noted. action items for customer:
- add our control-plane hostnames to their proxy allowlist (DIRECT / passthrough)
- if they cannot bypass MITM, import the proxy CA into the JVM truststore and ensure client certs are forwarded (not stripped)
- run and share `openssl s_client -connect controlplane.customer-redwood.example.com:443 -servername controlplane.customer-redwood.example.com -showcerts` and `curl --trace-ascii` output

mike_support: shared steps and the ticket. customer will try PAC -> DIRECT for the gateway and report back.
elaine_sre: thanks. if they hit 5xx after passthrough, ask them to include the raw `curl -v` handshake logs and we can check for SNI or backend routing issues. :thumbsup:
